correctness.rationale: For nonempty X in the nonempty-subset power semigroup, a nonzero product of s factors exists iff the directed support has a length-s walk; group labels cannot annihilate. A cycle prevents nilpotence, while a DAG with longest path length r−1 has least zero power r (the sole empty-support X={0} has index 1). The canonical levels by longest incoming path give immediately preceding-level nonempty parent sets and arbitrary edges that skip levels, yielding the displayed ordered-composition formula with each arrow weighted q=2^|G|−1 and a factor 2 for optional zero. The top layer and source inclusion-exclusion recurrence follow. Independent exhaustive DAG enumeration at n=2..4 and |G|=1,2 agrees for every index, including n=4,g=1 counts [1,172,528,384]. This finite test corroborates but does not replace the infinite proof. Caveat: counts individual nilpotent subsets, not nilpotent subsemigroups or arbitrary semigroups.
